I'm working on a fully memory-safe (LLVM) compiled Lisp dialect with a system Fω type system. Borrow checking is actually far more extensive than Rust and in fact all memory operations are required to be proven safe at compile time (either by the compiler, and if not possible, by the source code via appended proofs). Fairly stable at this point, in benchmark performance is tied with C/C++ even exceeding it because of more aggressive autovectorization and native vector types

For instance

   ; Sysv native vectors. Initializer values require matching [].
   (mut x (the v64 [10 20]))
   (set x (+ x 5))
   (at x 0 17)
   (print (at x 1))
   (print (all (= x (the v64 [17 25]))))

   ; Parameter and result types can be written inline
   (fn add4 ((a w64) (b w64)) -> w64 (+ a b))
   (let ((result (add4 (the w64 [1 2 3 4]) (the w64 [10 20 30 40]))))
      (print (at result 3)))
You also get full fp primitives

   ; helpers reused below
   (fn inc (x) (+ x 1))
   (fn dbl (x) (* x 2))
   (fn sq  (x) (* x x))
   (fn pair (a b) (+ a b))
   (fn add3 (a b c) (+ a b c))
   (fn dv (a b) (/ a b))
   (fn id (x) x)
   (fn zero (x) 0)

   ; |> : pipe a value left-to-right through functions.
   (print (|> 5 inc dbl sq))                ; => 144   (sq(dbl(inc 5)))

   ; >> : left-to-right compose; << : right-to-left compose.
   (print ((>> inc dbl) 5))                 ; => 12    (dbl(inc 5))
   (print ((<< dbl inc) 5))                 ; => 12    (dbl(inc 5))

   ; fmap / <$> : apply f, then g  (same as >>).
   (print ((fmap inc dbl) 5))               ; => 12
   (print ((<$> inc dbl) 5))                ; => 12    (11 on sysv: (inc (dbl 5)), function-first)

   ; <*> (and its alias <>) : the S combinator, (f x (g x)).
   (print ((<*> + (lambda (x) (+ x 2))) 5)) ; => 12    (5 + (5+2))

   ; <&> : flipped fmap, a(b x).      <**> : flipped S, (g x (f x)).
   (print ((<&> inc dbl) 5))                ; => 11    (inc(dbl 5))
   (print ((<**> (lambda (x) (+ x 2)) +) 5))   ; => 12 (5 + (5+2))
